name: Abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (Loft et al., 2026, Nature Met)
description: Abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies were collected from 14 individuals (7 men and 7 women) during severe obesity and after modest lifestyle-induced weight loss (8–10%) as well as substantial bariatric surgery–induced weight loss (20–45%). Patient samples at each time point were stratified into obese or normal weight based on their BMI.

labelsets.name: author_cell_type
labelsets.description: Annotation of all broad canonical cell populations present in AT were based on previously described markers from Loft et al. 2026 (PMID: 40360756).

labels.name: Adipocytes
labels.rationale: ADIPOQ and PLIN1 are established markers of mature adipocytes. ADIPOQ (adiponectin) is a hormone abundantly and selectively expressed by differentiated adipocytes and reflects their metabolic and endocrine function. PLIN1 (perilipin-1) is a lipid droplet–associated protein essential for lipid storage and lipolysis regulation, marking cells with mature adipocyte morphology. ADIPOQ and PLIN1 reliably identify differentiated adipocytes and distinguish them from stromal and progenitor cell populations.

labels.name: ASPCs
labels.rationale: PDGFRA and DCN are commonly used markers of adipose-derived stromal/progenitor cells (ASPCs). PDGFRA identifies mesenchymal stromal progenitors within adipose tissue and is enriched in cells with adipogenic potential. DCN (decorin) is an extracellular matrix proteoglycan highly expressed by stromal fibroblast-like cells and reflects the mesenchymal, matrix-producing identity of ASPCs. PDGFRA and DCN distinguish stromal/progenitor populations from mature adipocytes and endothelial or immune cells, supporting their use as markers of ASPCs.
synonyms: mesenchymal stem cell of adipose tissue

labels.name: ECs
labels.rationale: ADGRL4 (ELTD1) is an adhesion G protein–coupled receptor selectively expressed in vascular endothelial cells and is associated with angiogenic activity. MECOM is enriched in endothelial populations and has been implicated in endothelial cell identity and vascular development. MECOM and ADGRL4 support the identification of endothelial cells and help distinguish them from surrounding stromal and parenchymal cell types.

labels.name: Lymphoid immune cells
labels.rationale: IL7R (CD127) is expressed by T cells and other lymphoid populations and is critical for lymphocyte survival and homeostasis. CD3E is a core component of the T cell receptor complex and is selectively expressed in T lymphocytes. IL7R and CD3E identify lymphoid immune cell populations and distinguish them from myeloid and non-immune cells.

labels.name: Myeloid immune cells
labels.rationale: MRC1 (CD206) is a C-type lectin receptor expressed by macrophages and monocyte-derived cells, particularly those with a tissue-resident or alternatively activated phenotype. F13A1, encoding coagulation factor XIII A chain, is enriched in monocytes and macrophages and reflects myeloid lineage identity. MRC1 and F13A1 support the identification of myeloid immune cell populations and distinguish them from non-immune stromal and parenchymal cells.

labels.name: Pericytes
labels.rationale: STEAP family genes are enriched in mural cells and are associated with perivascular metal ion homeostasis and redox activity, a characteristic feature of pericytes. GIPR is selectively expressed in adipose tissue pericytes and marks a perivascular cell population closely associated with the microvasculature. Together, STEAP and GIPR support the identification of pericytes and help distinguish them from endothelial and stromal progenitor cells.

labels.name: SMCs
labels.rationale: MYOCD (myocardin) is a key transcriptional co-activator that drives smooth muscle differentiation and contractile gene expression. MYH11, encoding smooth muscle myosin heavy chain, is a definitive marker of differentiated, contractile SMCs. Together, MYOCD and MYH11 reliably identify smooth muscle cell populations and distinguish them from pericytes and other mesenchymal or stromal cells.

labels.name: Lymphatic ECs
labels.rationale: PROX1 is a master transcriptional regulator of lymphatic endothelial cell fate and is essential for lymphatic specification and maintenance. PKHD1L1 is enriched in lymphatic endothelial cells and has been identified as a marker distinguishing lymphatic from blood vascular endothelium.

labels.name: Mast cells
labels.rationale: KIT and CPA3 are canonical markers of mast cells. KIT (CD117) is a receptor tyrosine kinase essential for mast cell development, survival, and activation, and is highly expressed on mast cells. CPA3 (carboxypeptidase A3) is a mast cell–specific granule protease reflecting their secretory and effector function. KIT and CPA3 reliably identify mast cells and distinguish them from other immune cell populations.
